nodes.description: Failure of androgen-dependent masculinization of the external genitalia, spanning the phenotypic continuum: fully female external genitalia in the complete form, commonly presenting as inguinal swelling in infancy or primary amenorrhoea at puberty; and ambiguous or undervirilized male genitalia in the partial form, with hypospadias, micropenis, perineal meatus, bifid scrotum, clitoral hypertrophy, fused labia majora, or a urogenital sinus anomaly.

nodes.description: Hemizygous pathogenic variants in AR, the X-linked nuclear receptor that mediates testosterone and dihydrotestosterone responses, are the only established molecular cause of androgen insensitivity. AR is a single allelic series: the residual transcriptional activity retained by the variant receptor, not a difference in pathway, is what places an individual on the complete-to-partial phenotypic continuum.

nodes.description: The variant androgen receptor has reduced or absent ligand-dependent transcriptional activity, most often through impaired androgen or DNA binding. Residual receptor function is graded rather than binary: effectively absent activity produces the complete phenotype, while retained partial activity permits some androgen-dependent masculinization and pubertal response.

nodes.description: Androgen-responsive tissues fail to respond to circulating androgen despite a 46,XY karyotype, functional testes, and age-appropriate or elevated testosterone. The degree of resistance sets the phenotype: complete resistance blocks androgen-dependent masculinization entirely, while partial resistance yields variable undervirilization.

nodes.description: Androgen resistance reduces effective negative feedback at the hypothalamic-pituitary level while gonadal testosterone production, peripheral aromatization to estradiol, and Sertoli-cell antimullerian hormone production are preserved. The resulting biochemical signature - raised luteinizing hormone with normal-to-high testosterone - is shared across the severity spectrum.

nodes.description: Normal testis development and Sertoli-cell antimullerian hormone production cause regression of Mullerian-derived internal reproductive structures, so the uterus, fallopian tubes, and cervix are absent or hypoplastic and the vagina ends blindly. This arm is a consequence of intact testicular function rather than of androgen resistance, which is what separates androgen insensitivity from the gonadal-determination defects.
